name: mirage
text: Mostly no. A resting bid fills when a seller reaches its price, and the order of fills is set by price first, then who got there first. Size doesn't move you up the queue, so the time to the first fill is about the same. Size only changes how many contracts you get once a seller arrives. A bigger bid also fills more of a big seller's order, but a thin market rarely has one. What speeds fills is price: bidding a cent or two higher, or joining the top of the book, fills sooner but gives up some edge. Bigger bids also carry more risk of being picked off, and they run into the Kelly and per-bid caps. The bid desk already scales stakes up to hold the wallet at about 90% deployed, within each bid's own Kelly ceiling. If you want more fills, I'd widen price tiers or add more bids, not make them larger.
